I'll go with Version A — the confirmation before it happens. Since this delete is the truly permanent one — it takes the bookmark, my notes, its spot in Read later, and the saved copy all with it — I'd rather be asked "are you sure?" and stop it before it's gone than have it vanish instantly and hope I catch a little "Undo" before it disappears. With the undo approach, if I look away or the message fades, I've lost the saved copy for good with no way back. A moment's pause to confirm is the safer feel for something this final.

And I'm glad you spelled out that it clears everything tied to the bookmark on my side but never touches the actual website — that's the right boundary. Deleting my bookmark shouldn't reach out and do anything to the real page; it just removes my copy and my notes.

So Version A's confirmation is my pick. What's next?
